questions.question: STUDENT(sid, name, dept) is combined with DEPT(dept, building) by automatically pairing rows whose shared 'dept' values are equal — no ON condition is written and dept appears once in the result. Which operation is this?
questions.explanation: A natural join equates every pair of same-named attributes and keeps only one copy of each common column — here dept — in the result schema.

questions.question: A report must list every customer — including those who have never placed an order — with NULLs filling the order columns for the non-matching ones. Which join produces this?
questions.explanation: The left outer join preserves every tuple of the left relation and pads missing right-side attributes with NULL, so orderless customers still appear.

questions.question: EMP rows are paired with SALGRADE rows wherever EMP.sal BETWEEN SALGRADE.losal AND SALGRADE.hisal — the join uses a non-equality comparison. Which join type is this?
questions.explanation: A theta join pairs tuples satisfying an arbitrary comparison condition (here a BETWEEN range); equality-only conditions would make it an equijoin.

questions.question: The query expression { t | EMP(t) AND t.salary > 50000 } binds the variable t to entire rows of EMP. Which form of relational calculus is used?
questions.explanation: Tuple relational calculus ranges its variables over whole tuples, so t.salary refers to one attribute of the bound row.

questions.question: The expression { <n> | EXISTS s EXISTS d (EMP(<n, s, d>) AND s > 50000) } binds each variable to an individual attribute value rather than a row. Which form of relational calculus is this?
questions.explanation: Domain relational calculus ranges variables over attribute domains, composing tuples positionally like <n, s, d> instead of binding whole rows.

questions.question: To self-join EMP on its employee/manager columns, the algebra must give the same relation two different names — E1 and E2 — before joining. Which operator performs this renaming?
questions.explanation: The rename (rho) operator assigns new names to a relation or its attributes, a prerequisite for self-joins where both operands come from the same relation.

questions.question: From the relations STUDENTS and DEANS_LIST, a query keeps only the rows that appear in both. Which set operator does this?
questions.explanation: Intersection yields the tuples shared by two union-compatible relations — students who are also on the dean's list here.

questions.question: In a multi-step algebra solution, TEMP ← σ(salary > 50000)(EMP) stores the intermediate result under a new name so later steps can reference it. Which operation does the arrow denote?
questions.explanation: The assignment operation (←) names the result of an expression, letting complex algebra be written as a sequence of named intermediate relations.

questions.question: Knowing an EmpID always fixes exactly one employee name and one department — one attribute's value determines another's. What is this kind of constraint called?
questions.explanation: X → Y is a functional dependency when each value of X is associated with exactly one value of Y, as EmpID determines name and dept here.

questions.question: To test whether A is a superkey of R, you compute the complete set of attributes that A functionally determines and check that it covers all of R. What is that computed set called?
questions.explanation: The attribute closure A+ accumulates every attribute derivable from A by repeatedly applying the FDs; A is a superkey iff A+ contains all attributes of R.

questions.question: If relation R has 8 tuples and relation S has 5 tuples, how many tuples does R × S produce?
questions.explanation: The Cartesian product pairs each of the 8 tuples of R with each of the 5 tuples of S: 8 × 5 = 40.

questions.question: If relation R has 5 tuples, what is the minimum number of tuples in R LEFT OUTER JOIN S?
questions.explanation: A left outer join preserves every tuple of R, so the result contains at least 5 tuples even with no matches.

questions.question: How many attributes does the natural join of R(A, B, C) and S(C, D) produce?
questions.explanation: The common attribute C appears only once, so the result schema is (A, B, C, D) with 4 attributes.

questions.question: Relational calculus queries are built from predicates and the quantifiers ∃ and ∀ — they rest on which formal logic system?
questions.explanation: Relational calculus is a declarative language grounded in first-order predicate logic, whose quantifiers express 'there exists' and 'for all' over tuples or domain values.

questions.question: To express 'total salary per department' — grouping EMP by dept and applying SUM — relational algebra needs an extended operator that applies aggregate functions to groups of tuples. Which operator is it?
questions.explanation: The aggregation (generalized projection) operator of extended relational algebra groups tuples and applies functions like SUM, COUNT, and AVG to each group.

questions.question: R(A, B) = {(1, x), (2, y)} and S(B, C) = {(x, p), (z, q)}. How many tuples does the natural join R ⋈ S contain?
questions.explanation: Only the shared B value 'x' matches, producing the single tuple (1, x, p); 'y' and 'z' have no partners.

questions.question: The relational algebra expression sigma(B > 5) applied to pi(A, C)(R) is invalid. Which attribute is referenced by the selection but missing from the projection list?
questions.explanation: Projection pi(A, C) drops B from the schema, so a subsequent selection can no longer test B; the predicate must be applied before the projection.

questions.question: R(A, B, C) has 10 tuples and S(B, C, D) has 10 tuples. What is the maximum possible number of tuples in the natural join R ⋈ S?
questions.explanation: In the worst case every (B, C) value in R matches every (B, C) value in S, so the join can reach the Cartesian product size of 10 x 10 = 100.

questions.question: Deleting a row from ORDERS must automatically remove its rows in ORDER_LINES. Which referential action declared on the foreign key accomplishes this?
questions.explanation: ON DELETE CASCADE propagates the deletion to all referencing tuples, preserving referential integrity automatically.

questions.question: Executing R UNION S fails because R has three attributes while S has four. Which required property of the two relations is missing?
questions.explanation: Set operations require union compatibility: the same number of attributes with pairwise-compatible domains.
